title: Whether a second version of InferOps should proceed, as the data a test holds it to
description: The proceed, revise, or defer decision on a second version, made from V1's evidence rather than from a plan: the frozen evidence it rests on, the V1 findings it cites and the register rows behind each, the problems those findings expose with three separate questions answered for each, the options compared, the entry gates and their state, where every claim V1 does not certify is placed, the review date and triggers, and the published surface that still describes the repository before the decision. tests/testing/test_v2_investment_decision.py reads this file against the register, the evidence index, the case study's data, and the document, and fails when any of them disagrees. It holds the decision's references and consistency, never whether the reasoning is sound.

acceptedBy.act: Merging the change that carries this record. There is no other approval artifact.
acceptedBy.note: None of the four authorities in the decision-authority register is a decision about whether to open a new version: they cover architecture decisions, claim sign-off, and V1 release approval. The role that can merge is the one that accepts this record, and this record does not add an authority or change one.

decision.summary: Open no second version now. V1's own road is not yet closed for one workload, nobody but its author has walked it, and nobody outside the repository has reviewed it; the problem V1's evidence most strongly points at, a caller-visible outage caused by one replica, cannot be tested on the only host available. The next InferOps work, if any, is finishing V1's own claims inside its contract.

release.note: The annotated tag exists on the merge of V1-S5-008-PR1. The register is inside the frozen pack, so its release row still says no release has been executed; moving it is a change after the tag, under a new ledger, and this record does not make it.

findings.finding: From concurrency 1 to 4, completed requests stayed between 0.554 and 0.575 per second while median latency rose about fourfold; whether the single slot or the processor held the rate was not tested.

Losing the only serving pod under load caused a 31 960 ms caller-visible outage in which 40 of the 41 requests were refused; a second run's outage was 2 832 ms, and the record says one replica is the cause and says nothing about what a second would change.

At every readiness sample before the replacement was Ready, the deleted pod reported Ready while the Service had no ready endpoint, and scrape health still read the deleted pod up after the delete; two registered series are emitted by nothing, the collector keeps nothing past a release, and no alert has been evaluated by a Prometheus or delivered.

A model held from finishing its load stayed alive and unready for 179 755 ms without a restart, and no caller met model-not-ready, because the runtime's Service never held an address; the canonical-error claims stay planned.
Nothing turns a validated contract into release values; a values file is written by hand, and the two claims that would close the self-service loop are planned and hold no record.

The whole path completed from a fresh clone once, on its third attempt, by the change's author, an AI coding agent; no second engineer has repeated it, and the scaffold walkthrough was an independent AI reviewer rather than a human.
The multi-replica profile was refused at its capacity gate on the only host measured, before anything was installed; the gate was not weakened and the replica count was not reduced to fit.
In the first load run the request path used about 5.4 times the processor time it reserved while most of its memory reservation sat idle; the only prices are synthetic and nothing has been paid for.

No caller is authenticated or authorized and nothing is rate-limited; one experiment measured that the local cluster's network plugin enforces none of the rendered policy, and ten of the twelve carried risks block production use.
The one automated lane runs no cluster and no model; the rules for a real lane are published, no workflow for one is committed, and no runner is selected to hold the pinned model.

Every real result is one provider, one Windows host, CPU only, one replica of each tier; no record is above C2, nothing is C3 because no workload was declared representative before a run, and nothing can be C4 because there is no production operation to observe.

problems.problem: A workload owner can write and validate a contract, but nothing deploys what it describes; the paved road's own promise stops at a hand-written values file.

important.reason: It is the one step that makes the contract more than validated paper, and the case study calls it the most important unbuilt component in V1.

feasibleNow.reason: Rendering release values from a validated v1alpha1 document and serving from them needs the existing host, the existing chart, and no paid resource, and the claims that would move are already written.

belongs.reason: It finishes a claim V1 already states, inside the v1alpha1 contract, and changes no boundary rule.

problems.remainsUnproven: Any host or provider but the one measured, any workload shape the contract does not define, and anything about a generated workload a second person deployed.

problems.problem: Five more claims V1 states as planned have no record: the mock's self-identification, the two canonical errors, redaction in a real run, and no credential or model artifact in public history.

important.reason: Each is narrower than the road, but each is a promise V1 already publishes, and the unready-model run showed that one of them may not be reachable as written through the deployed topology.

feasibleNow.reason: Every one can be exercised on the existing host. A run may show that the model-not-ready claim cannot be met through the deployed topology, and restating it would then be the result.

belongs.reason: They are V1's own planned claims, inside the v1alpha1 contract.

problems.remainsUnproven: Whether any of them holds on another host or provider; a history scan is a static reading and reaches C0, not C2.

problems.problem: Whether a caller can be kept served while a serving pod is lost. V1 measured the outage one replica causes and could not measure what a second replica changes.

important.reason: It is the largest caller-visible effect V1 measured, and the only one whose cause its record names.

feasibleNow.reason: The only host measured fails the multi-replica capacity gate, and the difference is held by workloads that are not this project's to remove. Another host means other hardware or a paid provider, and neither is authorized or budgeted.

belongs.reason: How many replicas of its own release the platform runs, and what a caller meets when one is lost, is a property of this platform. It leaves this project the moment it becomes making the runtime answer more requests, which boundary rule 3 places elsewhere.

problems.remainsUnproven: A lost node, capacity, an availability figure, and any provider the experiment did not run on. C3 only if a representative intent and criteria are declared before the run.

problems.problem: Which signal tells an operator the truth during a failure, and whether it reaches anybody. Pod readiness and early scrape health described the lost pod, not what callers could reach, and no alert is evaluated in a release or delivered.

important.reason: An operator who trusts pod readiness during the pod-loss experiment is wrong for its whole outage, and a rule nobody evaluates tells nobody.

feasibleNow.reason: Emitting the two registered series nothing emits, evaluating the rules inside a release, and delivering to a local receiver need no new host. A durable store and alert routing are unowned and deferred out of V1 by ADR 0004 D7, so taking them on changes an accepted decision.

belongs.reason: Emitting series V1's own catalog registers is V1 completion. Evaluating, delivering, and keeping InferOps's own signals is a later version, because ADR 0004 D7 defers it. A telemetry backend other systems' telemetry flows into is a capability a workload declares through spec.integrations, which boundary rule 1 says this project does not provide.

problems.remainsUnproven: That an alert is acted on, or that a signal is right on a provider or topology not run.

problems.problem: Whether the single slot or the processor held the completed rate flat, which decides whether this setup's figure says anything about another.

important.reason: It is the question the load result left open, but answering it for one release does not make any figure portable.

feasibleNow.reason: A bounded rerun with more than one slot, processor throttling sampled, and a varied or uncached prompt mix needs the existing host and is permitted by ADR 0013 as a bounded observation.

belongs.reason: Naming what limited one declared release is a bounded observation this project may publish under ADR 0013. Raising throughput, batching, or capacity is work on the runtime's own behaviour, which boundary rule 3 places elsewhere, and sustained capacity stays deferred.

problems.remainsUnproven: Capacity, a benchmark, and any other runtime, model, host, or provider. No claim moves: sustained throughput and capacity stay deferred.

problems.problem: Whether the road works for anybody else, anywhere else. Every real result is one provider, one host, and one author, and the optional kind helper's only run names no revision.

important.reason: A reference path only its author has followed, on one machine, is not yet shown to be a reference for anybody.

feasibleNow.reason: A second person's run is not something the author can produce. Running on kind needs an install the maintainer declined for the release, and a non-Windows host needs other hardware.

belongs.reason: Reproducing V1 elsewhere is evidence about V1, not new scope, and ADR 0011 D2 already names kind as one of the two supported providers.

problems.remainsUnproven: Each new record certifies only its own host and provider; neither is read across to the other.

problems.problem: Whether anything in the platform refuses what it should: no caller is authenticated, nothing is rate-limited, no pod property is enforced, and the rendered network policy was measured inert on the local plugin.

important.reason: Nothing beyond one loopback host started by hand is possible while ten carried risks block production use.

feasibleNow.reason: An enforcing network plugin and pod admission can run on a local cluster. Caller identity and per-caller limits need a decision about where identity lives before anything is built.

belongs.reason: Enforcing policy and admitting pods for the platform's own releases belongs here, in a later version. Boundary rule 2 places a component in front of several providers elsewhere and does not settle who authenticates a single-provider API's own callers; that is an ADR 0004 question this record does not answer.

problems.remainsUnproven: That a deployed workload is defended, which no single record reaches, and enforcement on any plugin not run.

problems.problem: Every real result was produced by hand, because no lane can install a release or load a model.

important.reason: Without it a regression in real serving is found only when somebody runs it by hand.

feasibleNow.reason: It needs a runner authorized to hold the pinned model artifact, and ADR 0005 D6 and ADR 0012 leave that runner unselected.

belongs.reason: It is this project's own delivery, and it waits on the runner decision.

problems.remainsUnproven: Anything the lane does not run, on any runner it does not run on.

problems.problem: What running the workload costs on a provider. Every price in V1 is synthetic, and the finding that survived them is about use, not price.

important.reason: The useful cost finding, that reservation and use diverged in opposite directions, needed no price at all.

feasibleNow.reason: Nothing has ever been paid for, no provider account exists, and an account and a budget would need authorization.

belongs.reason: An actual-basis record for InferOps's own release belongs here: the method exists and is tested. Accelerator economics is work on the runtime's hardware, which boundary rule 3 places elsewhere.

problems.remainsUnproven: Any cost but the one provider, window, and rate card read; paying a provider is not production operation.

problems.problem: Whether any result represents intended use. Nothing is C3, because no workload or infrastructure was declared representative, with criteria, before a run.

important.reason: It is the only way to change a level rather than repeat one, and a higher level is not better evidence for every claim.

feasibleNow.reason: V1 declared no intended use beyond a contributor's own machine, so the first step is a decision about what to represent, not a run.

belongs.reason: Declaring an intended use widens what V1 is for, which is a decision for a version rather than a completion of this one.

problems.remainsUnproven: Behaviour outside the declared distribution and anything C4 would say: there is no organizational production to observe, so that claim cannot move on C3 alone.

entryGates.gate: A first versioned release is cut over the frozen evidence pack.
entryGates.evidence: The annotated tag v1.0.0 exists on the merge of V1-S5-008-PR1. The register inside the pack still lists a published release as not claimed, and moving that row is owed as a change after the tag.

entryGates.gate: Real runtime and failure evidence exists for the road V1 built.
entryGates.evidence: C2 records for the load matrix, the pod loss, the unready model, and the clean-clone run.

entryGates.gate: One workload is served from its validated contract alone, so a second version would widen a road that exists.
entryGates.evidence: Both claims are planned and hold no record; release values are written by hand.

entryGates.gate: Somebody other than the author has completed the clean-clone journey from its own page.
entryGates.evidence: The claim's limitation: one run, by the change's author; no second engineer has repeated it.

entryGates.gate: Somebody outside the repository has reviewed a claim, a record, or the release, and whatever need they name is weighed here.
entryGates.evidence: The release notes and the register both state that no outside party has reviewed anything; every approval is the repository-maintainer role's, which has one holder.

entryGates.gate: A proceed, revise, or defer decision is recorded with its evidence.
entryGates.evidence: This record, once the change carrying it is merged.

options.summary: Open a second version now, take V1's road as complete for one workload, and widen it to further workload shapes and the operations V1 left unowned.
options.problemAddressed: Whether the contract generalizes beyond one workload profile.
options.motivation: No V1 finding motivates it. The contract refuses an asynchronous profile by design, which records a choice, not a measured need.
options.expectedEvidence: C2 for a second profile, on the same host and provider: a new claim that is still one setup.
options.prerequisites: Every unmet entry gate, including a road that deploys one workload from its contract.
options.costsAndRisks: It builds generality on a deployment step written by hand, and every result would again be one host, one provider, one replica: the kind of evidence the case study says would not justify a second version.
options.remainsUnproven: Everything the pod-loss, capacity-gate, telemetry, and security findings left open, and the self-service road itself.
options.overlap: Further workload shapes cross no boundary rule, and none answers a V1 finding.
options.why: Refused: three entry gates are unmet, and its problem is not one V1's evidence exposed.

options.summary: Open a second version now, with its problem restated from V1's evidence: keeping a caller served, and an operator told the truth, when a serving pod is lost.
options.problemAddressed: The one-replica outage and the signals that misdescribed it, together.
options.motivation: The largest caller-visible effect V1 measured, the disagreement between pod readiness and the Service during it, and the gate that stopped a second replica being tried.
options.expectedEvidence: C2 on a host that passes the capacity gate, certifying only that host; C3 only if a representative intent and acceptance criteria are declared before the run.
options.prerequisites: A host that passes the multi-replica capacity gate, authorized and budgeted if it is paid for; an amendment to ADR 0004 D7 for alert delivery and a durable store; and every unmet entry gate.
options.costsAndRisks: Hardware or provider spend that is not authorized, and drift: redundancy turns into autoscaling and throughput, which boundary rule 3 places elsewhere.
options.remainsUnproven: A lost node, capacity, an availability figure, production operation, and any provider not run.
options.overlap: Deeper serving work, if it widens from redundancy to throughput or autoscaling; a telemetry backend for other systems, if it widens from InferOps's own signals.
options.why: Not now: its problem is the right one, but three entry gates are unmet and the host it needs is not available. It is kept as the problem statement a later proposal starts from.

options.summary: Open no second version now. The next InferOps work, if any, finishes V1's own claims inside the v1alpha1 contract; the revised problem statement is held for the review.
options.problemAddressed: The self-service road and V1's other planned claims, and a second person walking the road.
options.motivation: V1 publishes seven planned claims and a road that stops before deployment, and only its author has followed it.
options.expectedEvidence: C2 on the existing host for claims V1 already states: new claims reaching a record, not repeats of the same one.
options.prerequisites: None beyond the existing host for the planned claims. A second person's run and an outside review cannot be produced by the author, and are waited for, not scheduled.
options.costsAndRisks: The largest caller-visible effect V1 measured stays unaddressed until the review, and a reviewer may reasonably weigh it above closing the road first.
options.remainsUnproven: Everything the one-replica, signal, rate-limit, security, lane, price, and representative problems name.
options.overlap: None: all of it is inside V1's boundary and contract.
options.why: Selected: it is the only option no unmet gate refuses, and it answers findings V1 published rather than a plan.

uncertifiedClaims.whyNotPlaced: It is about how V1's records were written, and neither motivates nor blocks a second version. Closing it means new records, because the frozen ones are not edited.

reviewTriggers.trigger: Both planned contract claims are certified, so one workload is served from its contract alone.
A second person completes the clean-clone journey, or somebody outside the repository reviews a claim, a record, or the release.
A host that passes the multi-replica capacity gate, or an authorized budget for one, becomes available.
Feedback from outside the repository names a need this record does not list.

describesTheRepositoryBeforeThisDecision.says: Whether a second version proceeds, and what it contains, is a separate decision that has not been made, and nothing here assumes it.
describesTheRepositoryBeforeThisDecision.why: The case study is bound to the frozen evidence digests and stays as published. This record is that separate decision.
